documented: Contentful personal access tokens authenticate to the Content Management API; its official SDK declares the content_management_manage scope and separates the token secret from sys.id.
The provider's SCIM FAQ shows Bearer CFPAT- as the personal-access-token authentication form.
assumptions: The case-sensitive CFPAT- prefix and 43-character ASCII-alphanumeric, underscore or hyphen body follow Titus v1.2.9's PAT scanner subset. The body width is not claimed to be an exhaustive issuer grammar or inferred from a sample as a provider guarantee.

Only prefixed management PAT candidates are covered. Unprefixed delivery, preview and OAuth values are excluded because this rule cannot establish their scope from their bodies; this does not claim that all excluded values are public or harmless.
Native right boundaries reject accepting a fixed-length prefix of a longer credential; no entropy, cryptographic, issuer or live authorization check is added.
evidence.fixture_method: Deterministic synthetic 43-character bodies, including underscore/hyphen terminal characters and a letters-only body. Bare, Bearer, assignment, JSON and adjacent-token carriers are paired with case, length, alphabet, suffix and public-ID/unprefixed delivery-preview controls. No live credentials.

documented: PostHog personal API keys must be kept private and authenticate to private endpoints. Its API documentation identifies phx_ as the personal-key prefix and distinguishes public project-token endpoints.
The pinned 2024 generator encodes 35 random bytes as an unpadded base62 integer after phx_; its body width varies and can reach 48 characters.

The pinned 2026 generator sets the top bit of 35 random bytes and uses base57 excluding 0, 1, O, I and l. Integer encoding can yield 48 or 49 characters; the create/roll endpoints call this generator.
The generator assigns phc_ to public project tokens and distinct phs_, pha_ and phr_ prefixes to other credentials. These are not this personal-key rule.
assumptions: The 43-character minimum is a conservative candidate bound from TruffleHog v3.97.4, not a generator minimum. Shorter historical integer encodings are not claimed to be invalid.

The ASCII-alphanumeric 43-49-character candidate range covers the pinned base62/base57 forms without importing upstream scanners' unsupported underscore/hyphen body alphabet. It does not validate canonical integer range, issuance, scope, entropy or future token revisions.
Native case-sensitive prefix and credential-alphabet right boundaries reject longer opaque values and avoid broadening this rule to public phc_ or the separately scoped phs_/pha_/phr_ families.
evidence.fixture_method: Deterministic synthetic generator-shaped examples: encode bytes 0 through 34 with the high bit set in historical base62 and current base57; encode the maximum 280-bit integer in base57 to exercise the 49-character upper width. A letters-only 43-character candidate exercises the documented scanner lower bound. Bare, Bearer and JSON positives accompany case, length, alphabet, boundary, masked/public-ID and excluded-prefix negatives. No live keys or network verification.
